summary.headline: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 volumes flat YoY; normalised consolidated EBITDA margin 7% after inventory write-downs, with Q2 guided to double-digit YoY volume growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was soft: total sales volume was flat YoY as PVC resin prices fell Rs.32/kg in April and Rs.5/kg in June, hitting primary and secondary demand in April. Normalised consolidated business EBITDA margin was 7% (Apollo standalone 8%, Kisan standalone 6%), with the gap to reported numbers mostly inventory write-downs, plus about 0.5% cost from new businesses (Varanasi plant and Window profiles). Management says prices have stabilised since a MIP of $766/MT (about Rs.82/kg) was imposed about 12 days before the call, and expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and H2 better than H1. Management maintained high double-digit volume growth ambition and reiterated 7-8% business EBITDA margin for the next 12-15 months.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost drag from new businesses (Varanasi, Window profiles) at Apollo standalone

financial_highlights.change: Unchanged vs FY26 end and Q1 June 2026

segments.name: Construction (PVC pipes)
segments.commentary: Construction is about 60% of sales; management expects construction demand to take over from agri as the main driver of sales momentum after monsoon.

segments.name: Kisan (West / Maharashtra plant)
segments.commentary: Business EBITDA about 5-6% but reported P&L shows losses; volume flat at about 5,500 tons per quarter for four quarters, versus nearly 7,000 tons in Q4 FY26. Plant capacity is 8,000-8,500 tons per quarter; Tarapur plant to serve Maharashtra and neighbouring states.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: Grew YoY in Q1 despite flat company volumes, following the Lubrizol tie-up; co-branding and co-marketing under way and expected to be a major contributor to high double-digit growth.

segments.name: Window profiles
segments.commentary: Targeted at 7-8% of revenue in FY27, rising to about 10% at full utilisation of current capacity; ramping up as a direct D2C offering.

segments.name: Government infrastructure (O-PVC, HDPE)
segments.commentary: Volume at almost zero YoY and a major drag on overall volumes; no pick-up in government disbursements yet under Nal Se Jal.

segments.name: Other product lines
segments.commentary: Water tanks growing double-digit, fittings single-digit growth, bath fittings flat.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 volume growth expected to be double-digit YoY and better than Q1 on QoQ basis; H2 FY27 expected to be much better than H1.
FY27 volume growth expected to be double-digit; high double-digit volume growth maintained for the coming years.
Business EBITDA margin of 7-8% targeted for the next 12-15 months, with a further 50-100 bps improvement expected as Varanasi and Window profile plants stabilise.
Varanasi plant (about Rs.300 crore revenue capacity) targeted at 30% utilisation in FY27, then 50-60% in FY28, 70% in FY28 and balance in FY29.

Long-term FY31 goal: four large plants each generating Rs.800-1,000 crore revenue at 10%+ EBITDA margin, plus new products to reach about Rs.1,000 crore revenue in four years; also cited Rs.5,000 crore top line over five years at 25% ROC.
Working capital: target net working capital days of 30 (currently 45), with debtor days to 25 by FY27-end or H1 FY28, and release of 10-15 days eventually.
Kisan merger scheme already filed; expected cost synergies of about 1% at company level.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs.200 crore across FY27 and FY28 (about Rs.100 crore each year), funded from operating cash flow; covers pending Varanasi, Brownfield expansions and new products.
Longer-term capex of Rs.600-700 crore over five years, 70-80% from internal cash flow; management says no debt or equity raise needed for ongoing capex.
South India: land acquisition to be completed in FY27, with plant construction to start from Q2 FY28 subject to Varanasi and Kisan Maharashtra ramp-up milestones; can be fast-tracked.
Kisan Maharashtra (Tarapur) plant to be the focus for Maharashtra and neighbouring states after plant shutdowns within Kisan.
demand_pricing: PVC resin prices fell about 30% in the first 20 days of April (Rs.32/kg fall), with a further Rs.5/kg fall in June; prices stabilised in May-June.

MIP of $766/MT (about Rs.82/kg on export basis) imposed about 12 days before the call; market price is at or 1-2% above the reliance price, and management expects prices to stay stable with limited downside.
Channel partners are cautious and holding low inventory; restocking expected if price stability holds for 10-15 days.
Monsoon expected to soften demand for the next 15-20 days; construction expected to pick up strongly post-monsoon.
Management claims market share gains, given flat volumes in a contracting industry while smaller players faced disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of recently imposed MIP on PVC pricing and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: MIP of $766/MT (about Rs.82/kg) applied about 12 days earlier; market is at or slightly above reliance price, so prices expected to stay stable with a floor set by MIP.

qa_highlights.question: What one-offs related to new businesses were in Q1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Upfront costs for Varanasi ramp-up and salary costs for building a Window profile ground team; the new businesses cost about 0.5% of Apollo standalone margin, and the rest of the margin gap was inventory write-down.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-8% margin achievable near term given competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said business margin was 8% at Apollo and 6-7% at Kisan before inventory losses; expects to maintain 7-8% at company level, with 50-100 bps upside as new plants stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the inventory loss in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure, saying the majority of the gap between the 7% normalised margin and reported EBITDA was inventory losses.

qa_highlights.question: Is PVC resin availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Recent delays were due to port rains delaying container de-stuffing, not supply shortage; material normally arrives within about 10 days and importers are returning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kisan volume and profitability picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume flat at about 5,500 tons per quarter for four quarters, versus nearly 7,000 tons in Q4 FY26; plant can do 8,000-8,500 tons per quarter; business EBITDA about 5-6% but reported P&L is weaker due to inventory losses and weak industry.

qa_highlights.question: Segment volume growth and return ratio math?
qa_highlights.answer: No segment-level growth given; CPVC and water tanks growing, government infra near zero. Return math kept: Rs.1,500 crore gross block plus Rs.300-400 crore working capital on Rs.5,000 crore revenue at 10-12% EBITDA gives about 25% ROC.

risks_watch: Restocking timing: distributors are holding low inventory and management says restocking starts only if price stability holds for about 10-15 days; Q2 double-digit YoY growth depends on it.
Inventory write-downs: management did not quantify the Q1 loss beyond saying most of the gap to reported EBITDA was inventory losses; further write-downs are possible if MIP-supported prices soften.
Government infrastructure (O-PVC, HDPE) near zero YoY with no disbursement pickup under Nal Se Jal yet; management hopes for activity in the next three to four months.
Kisan volumes flat at about 5,500 tons per quarter for four quarters versus nearly 7,000 tons in Q4 FY26; reported P&L still loss-making, and the Kisan merger scheme is pending.
Ramp-up milestones for Varanasi (30% utilisation in FY27) and the Tarapur plant gate the timing of the South India plant (construction from Q2 FY28) and the 50-100 bps margin upside.
Working capital: inventory at 80 days and net working capital at 45 days versus a 30-day target; debtor-day reduction to 25 depends on cash-and-carry schemes in South and West India.

So, we are fairly confident that FY27, we will be doing double-digit volume growth.
Right now, the company is almost net cash.

summary.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and the 7-8% margin range, but cautious on near-term numbers: Q1 was described as soft and April as the worst month, and management declined to quantify inventory losses or segment growth. Tone on government demand and Kisan's reported profitability was more hedged, with recovery repeatedly tied to post-monsoon construction and price stability.
